_comment: The joint-limit gate, spelled out as its own profile.
Since 2026-10-27 this is also the SHIPPED default (configs/scanner_trackscan49.json),
so this file is kept as the explicit, self-documenting way to ask for it.
Design: docs/2026-10-22-j5-overtravel-kinematics-gate-design.md (sections 4, 5, 12).
scanplan plan --station input/station_fixed.json --config configs/robot_gate.json --out output/robot
What changes when this is on:
* a pose the arm cannot hold with joint_margin_deg to spare is rejected BEFORE the
selection, so the reported coverage describes poses that can actually be commanded;
* a stroke that leaves the envelope halfway along stops growing there;
* the delivered points carry a joint solution, and the .LS CONFIG string for each point
comes from that solution instead of the constant `N U T, 0, 0, 0`;
* the report grows a `kinematics` block with the J5 distribution, the branch histogram
and the worst joint step.
Before using this as an acceptance criterion, close the three site gaps in section 11.2
of the design:
G1 the real soft limits (the values in the shipped robot block are INFERRED),
G2 what the CONFIG letters mean on this controller (the letters are emitted as hints),
G3 whether ROBOGUIDE is configured with the datasheet limits (+-250 on J5) rather than
the controller's (+-125) - if it is, every simulation verdict about reachability is
void.
`--joint-blocks` on `scanplan ls` goes one step further and writes P[n] as joint angles,
which removes the controller's branch choice entirely. It relies on the model being
right (position residual 0.02 mm over six measured poses), so try it on a handful of
points before a whole program.
